intro: Entries, tastings and scores: how a baking contest is told in Spanish.
p.apuntarse.nota: Always followed by a: me apunto a.
b1.texto:
**Before.** The organisers **convocan un concurso**: **de repostería**, **de cocina** or **de pasteles**. Each contestant chooses **una receta**, buys the ingredients and trains. The neighbours **comentan** who will win. The day before is **el día de descanso**, when nobody is allowed to practise.

**The day.** Each **concursante** goes to **la cocina del concurso**, puts on **el delantal**, mixes the dough with **la batidora** and puts the cake in **el horno**. You can also **rendirte**, **repetir la receta** or **pedir más tiempo**. The number of people who come is **la asistencia**; the rest stay at home.

**After.** The tastings become **puntos**. A cake with the top score is **la ganadora**. If two cakes have the same score, they **empatan** and there is **un empate**. The others are **los finalistas**.

**The tasters.** In the village, **los catadores** sit at **la mesa grande** and **los pasteleros** wait in **la cocina**. Together they are **el concurso**.

**The three steps.** **La masa**, **el horno** and **la decoración**.

**Losing heart.** A contestant **se rinde**. A cake falls after **un mal horneado**. A day when everything goes wrong is **un desastre**, and what follows is **una segunda oportunidad**.

**Verbs with prepositions.** **Apuntarse a** un concurso, **presentarse a** una prueba, **pertenecer a** un club, **encargarse de** la nata.
b2.f0: At eight in the evening the ovens were switched off and one of the longest nights in memory began.
b2.f1: The hall had filled to seventy per cent, five points more than the organisers had announced.
b2.f2: With half the cakes tasted, none was getting close to the top score.
b2.f3: The neighbourhood pastry chef had lost ten points, but was still the most applauded.
b2.f4: Shortly before midnight, the most veteran taster announced that she was willing to reward anyone who respected the original recipe.
b2.f5: Nobody gave up that night, although more than one contestant ran out of cream.
b2.f6: The organisers agree that, unless the tie is settled, the final will have to be repeated before the summer.
b4.pregunta: According to the text, did any cake get the top score?
b4.o0.refuerzo: Ninguna se acercaba a la máxima puntuación.
b4.o2.refuerzo: Only half the cakes had been tasted by then.
b5.pregunta: According to the text, what will happen if the tie is not settled?
b5.o1.refuerzo: Giving up is a distractor; the question asks what happens if the tie stays.
b5.o2.refuerzo: Deciding is a distractor; the question asks about repeating the final instead.
b6.pregunta: The appliance that bakes the cake is…
b7.pregunta: Complete: I always sign up for the same contest.
b7.o2.refuerzo: The usual form is apuntarse a.
b8.pregunta: Complete: unless the tie is settled…
b8.o0.refuerzo: A menos que takes the subjunctive.
b8.o1.refuerzo: A menos que takes the subjunctive.
b8.o2.refuerzo: A menos que takes the subjunctive.
b9.o0.explicacion: Se ha rendido means has given up and stopped competing.
b9.o2.explicacion: Rendirse is to give up of one's own will.
b10.traduccion: The organisation has called the final for May.
b11.texto:
**The app cannot check this part.** For the writing, please use pen and paper. For the speaking, say it out loud and, if you can, practise with a native speaker or a teacher who can correct you.

**Write (150–180 words).** Write a description of a contest you took part in or watched: preparation, surprises and result.

**Speak (about 3 minutes).** Explain aloud why many people enjoy competitions, and whether it is better to compete alone or in a team.
